title: Schema-driven metric enrichment and cardinality control for inference ingest
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current metrics ingestion path for inference traffic allows high-cardinality labels (route_id, prompt_hash, customer_model_variant) to proliferate into Prometheus and long-term storage. This increases cost and makes SLO bucketing noisy. We need an ingest-stage solution that enforces a schema, enriches lightweight inference KPIs, and applies per-customer cardinality profiles before metrics are persisted or forwarded.

Goal: Implement a schema-driven enrichment layer in the metrics-gateway that: 1) validates and normalizes OTLP/Prometheus envelopes, 2) performs deterministic label trimming and computed fields (inference_latency_bucket, token_cost_estimate), 3) applies per-customer cardinality policies (trim, aggregate, sample), and 4) supports transparent toggles and audit logs so customers can opt into higher-cardinality retention. The system should be resilient, add minimal latency, and be observable itself.

Scope: Ingest path only (metrics-gateway + remote_write adapter + OTel proxy). Does not include UI changes for Console dashboards (follow-up).

Design notes: We will introduce a lightweight "metric schema registry" (JSON Schema v1) stored in S3 and cached in memory. The gateway will perform: schema validation, enrichment (derive inference_latency_bucket: p50/p90/p99 cutoffs based on model family), label canonicalization, delta-encoding for high-cardinality counters, and cardinality-reduction policies (hash bucketing or sample-on-write). For Prometheus remote_write, we will add a shard key based on customer_id for better downstream distribution. Backpressure: use a bounded queue with configurable token-bucket and fail-open policy with sampled drops recorded to a separate telemetry stream.

Why different: Existing efforts focus on raw KPI ingestion and OTLP harmonization; this ticket focuses on active enrichment + cardinality control with per-customer profiles and auditability to reduce long-term costs while preserving SLO fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway validates and applies schema to incoming OTLP/Prometheus envelopes and logs schema violations to the debug stream
End-to-end latency overhead for metric ingestion <= 6ms p50 under normal load and <= 15ms p50 under burst test (100k metrics/s)
Cardinality reduction of at least 60% for selected high-card customers in staged rollout (measured via compare job)
Per-customer profile can be toggled via config and changes take effect within 90s without gateway restart
All policy-driven label trimming and computed fields are recorded in an audit log and visible in the gateway debug trace
Automated integration tests for schema registry refresh, shard routing, and sampled-drop telemetry exist and pass in CI
